## 2. Story question

How does the Botanist keep a dying light from becoming a comforting metaphor when wheat and barley depend on it?

## 3. Verified source record

The complete JSON entry below is copied from the current local source. Preserve its id, author_id, author_name, day, hour, knowledge_key, timestamp, and exact text. Candidate prose is editorial material, not part of the loaded row.

```json
{
  "id": "journal_raw_b3_23_botanist_the_flicker",
  "text": "The bulb is flickering. I am writing this in the greenhouse at 06:00 with the light on and the light is not steady. It is a small flicker — a half-second dim, then bright, then dim. A bulb that flickers is a bulb that is dying. I have known this since the first greenhouse I worked in, which was not this one, which had lights that did not flicker, which had a power grid, which had a world. The flicker is in the filament or the ballast or the connection and I do not know which and it does not matter which because the bulb is the last one and there is no second one and the LED retrofit the Electrician built is 5 percent and 5 percent is not a greenhouse. 5 percent is a candle. The wheat seedlings are on bed B under the flickering bulb. The barley is on bed B under the flickering bulb. I put them on the same bed because I will not split a dying light between two beds. They share it or they lose it together. That is the decision I made at 05:00. The Teacher would say it is a metaphor. It is not a metaphor. It is a bulb. I am a botanist. I grow things under lights. The light is dying. I will not pretend the light is not dying. I will document the flicker. I will document the hours the bulb holds. I will document the moment it fails. And then I will move the wheat seedlings to the LED array and I will watch them survive at 5 percent, which is not thriving, which is surviving, which is the thing the wheat does because the wheat is the proof and the proof outlives the practice. Suki said that. I said it to the council. I said I can accept it. I did not say I accept it gracefully. I do not accept it gracefully. I accept it the way a person accepts a season turning. The season is turning. The bulb is flickering. I am writing it down.",
  "timestamp": "Day 188, 06h",
  "author_name": "The Botanist",
  "author_id": "the_botanist",
  "knowledge_key": "grow_light_flickering_last_bulb",
  "day": 188,
  "hour": 6.0
}
```

## 4. Fixed canon and open space

The last working bulb flickers over wheat and barley together on bed B. The LED retrofit is at five percent; the Botanist plans to document the bulb’s hours and move wheat to the array if the bulb fails. No failure time or crop result is recorded here. Do not turn “the bulb” into an omen or assert the seedlings survive. Candidate language may add an image, rhythm, or private impression as an editorial draft, but no proposed addition becomes a further remembered event or confirmed fact until the existing content owner selects and reviews it against the source.

The source voice is The Botanist. The Botanist insists on material evidence: a half-second dim, a shared bed, a five-percent array, and a record of the failure when it comes. Preserve anger and acceptance without pretending the light is a symbol to the person doing the work. The prose may notice what the author can count, hear, repair, fear, or leave uncertain, while keeping the account’s limits visible.
